description:
FILED s539 (reviewing session, 2026-11-12) from the pre-review probes of s538a (#3554).  PRE-EXISTING: main 23f0f917 and the s538a tree (cf5c264f) print the same two lines.  Not held against the batch (it fixed what `_` holds; the die is in the right place with perl's exit status).

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3; ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s539/review/c/p2.pl line 14 + .perl/.main/.tree):

    symlink "/tmp", "/tmp/l$$"; print -l -e "/tmp/l$$";     # the stacked form: -e stats, then -l _

  perl:  The stat preceding -l _ wasn't an lstat at p2.pl line 14.          (rc 9)
  PCL:   While evaluating the form starting at line 99, column 0
           of #P"/tmp/runpcl_178172.lisp":The stat preceding -l _ wasn't an lstat      (rc 9)

The error is signalled with a plain CL `error`, not through the perl-shaped die path, so it carries no location (the #1240 registers hold it) and the uncaught printer shows the load note.  The USER's rule (s494): fail in the same place and be TIDY -- one readable line.  Family: #2108 / #1595 / #1970 (untidy uncaught errors); s538a notes the same site reports `(eval 0) line 0` when caught.  Fix: raise it through the die helper the other run-time fatals use; check the siblings in the stat / filetest code for the same raw `error`.  LOW.
subject: TIDY: the uncaught die "The stat preceding -l _ wasn't an lstat" is a raw CL error -- no ` at FILE line N.`, and it prints the loader's "While evaluating the form starting at line 99 ... of #P\"/tmp/runpcl_N.lisp\"" note (perl: one line with the location; same place, same exit status 9)
